title: Opportunity Cost Awareness
equation: True Cost = Direct + Best Alternative Lost
hook: That $500 project didn't cost me $500. It cost me the $1,200 client I didn't have time for.
statement: Every yes is a hidden no to something else. The real cost includes what you gave up.
explainer: Price tags only show half the cost. The other half is the best thing you couldn't do because your time or money was already spoken for.
sop: List your top 3 time or money commitments.
For each, name the best alternative you're giving up.
Put a number on the Direct cost and the Best Alternative Lost.
Add them up and compare the True Cost to what it's returning.
Drop or renegotiate the one where True Cost clearly wins.
equation_example: Direct cost $500, Best Alternative Lost $1,200. $500 + $1,200 = $1,700 True Cost. Higher means the decision cost way more than the price tag. Lower means the price tag was close to honest.
question: Write down one yes you're keeping and the better thing it's quietly costing you.
closing_statement: The price tag is never the whole cost.
caption:
Principle Nº 153: Opportunity Cost Awareness

That $500 project didn't cost me $500. It cost me the $1,200 client I didn't have time for.

Every yes is a hidden no to something else. The real cost includes what you gave up.

Your turn: Write down one yes you're keeping and the better thing it's quietly costing you.
